Hi Irene / Redwood team,

Thanks for the redline. A couple of items procurement flagged that we need clarity on before we can sign:

1) Escrow/holdback trigger: the Order Form currently references a $500k escrow threshold for IP infringement remediation. Procurement is asking whether that can be lowered or tiered (e.g., lower threshold for customer-impacting claims).

2) Evidence ownership & handoff: we need to confirm the evidence collection and ownership process if a third-party claim arises. Specifically: who collects bit-for-bit artifacts from running models and who retains them for the duration of litigation? Would Redwood be willing to accept a limited evidence-steward role with a signed affidavit that we can present to counsel?

3) Defense control vs. reimbursement: the MSA draft gives Redwood the right to assume defense but requires customer cooperation. Can you confirm whether Redwood will commit to step-in counsel and an escalation path (technical liaison + weekly status updates) for high-severity claims?

Attached: our latest Order Form and a procurement checklist. Weeding through redlines now — will aim to consolidate commercial asks into a single list.

Can we get an internal view from legal on (1) whether the $500k is negotiable and (2) what evidence-handling options Redwood can offer?

Thanks,

Sara Lane

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Legal and Risk.

Short answers up front, then details:
- Escrow threshold: Redwood is willing to discuss a tiered threshold tied to remediation type; recommended baseline $250k for indemnifiable IP remediation tied to third-party claims (we can split remediation vs. defense costs).
- Evidence handling: Redwood can act as an evidence custodian for technical artifacts (logs, model binaries, training/fine-tune manifests) under a documented chain-of-custody. We would require a technical-affidavit process and reasonable legal instructions before handing over sensitive artifacts.
- Defense control: Redwood prefers to retain the right to manage defense for IP claims to control litigation strategy, but we can commit to weekly technical-counsel syncs and an agreed escalation path for cases exceeding $1M exposure where joint counsel can be considered.

Proposed compromise (high level):
1) Limit Redwood indemnity to third-party IP infringement claims arising from Redwood-delivered models or services (carve out customer-provided prompts/data misuse).
2) Set escrow/holdback at $250k for remediation; above that, require insurance/offset language and a good-faith escrow replenishment plan.
3) Evidence handoff: Redwood to collect artifacts and hold them for 90 days post-notice, provide a certified technical-affidavit, and produce for-counsel copies under a protective order.

I asked Ben (claims lead) to draft a short redline that captures this compromise and a suggested addendum with a chain-of-custody template.

Irene Choi
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

Team / Sara — drafted a concise alternative that I think balances risk. Top-level bullets for procurement to review, then I'll drop a redline in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/ords/Orchid/proposed-indemnity-redline.docx

- Scope: Redwood indemnifies for third-party claims that allege direct infringement by Redwood-delivered models or code; explicit carveouts for (i) Customer custom prompts that materially change behavior, (ii) Customer-provided data that introduces third-party content, (iii) Open-source components disclosed in Appendix A.
- Defense vs. Reimbursement: Redwood retains Right to Defend; however, if Customer reasonably rejects appointed counsel within 10 business days, Customer may elect to control defense and Redwood will reimburse documented defense costs up to the applicable cap.
- Escrow / remediation: Propose a two-tier holdback: $150k for operational remediation (patches, model rollbacks), $500k for adjudicated damages or settlement payments. While this looks higher, we agree to an auto-escalation path where Redwood will mobilize insurance and a replenishment discussion occurs at $250k.
- Evidence custody: Redwood will collect and retain technical artifacts for 180 days after notice, preserve hash-sums, and provide a signed technical-affidavit to Customer counsel. Production of raw artifacts requires either a stipulated protective order or a court order; we will provide sanitized extracts earlier for triage.
- Insurance offset: Claims may be subject to insurance offset; propose clause clarifying interaction with current policy (will share summary with procurement).

I'll attach the redline and a one-page chain-of-custody template. Can Legal confirm the proposed 180-day evidence hold and two-tier escrow? Also confirm whether the reimbursement fallback language is acceptable.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference
